thread:
IncidentBot: [P0] automatic pager — increased error rate and streaming stalls detected from runtime group kv-cache + continuous-batching subsystem. Pager created: 1824501234.

Alex Chen: I'm on it. Seeing a sharp memory growth on kv-cache workers in us-west-2, followed by token cadence stalls on streaming requests.

Maria Gonzalez: Thanks. Can you post the alerts? I see: `kv_cache_mem > 85%` and `streaming_partial_flush_errors` spike to 5xx. Customers reporting truncated streams.

Alex Chen: Paste of the alert graph -> https://grafana.internal/r/xyz (shortlink). Key points: kv cache entry count doubled in ~3m; batch latencies jumped from 12ms -> 180ms.

Sam Patel: Leaving a note: I deployed the new batching heuristics yesterday (commit `0f3a1b7`), it's the primary suspect. That change altered the eviction/pinning heuristics which might cause cache blowups under certain prefix distributions.

Lee Park: Paging behavior looks like cascade: cache memory climbs -> eviction thrash -> batching groups shrink -> continuous-batching timeouts -> streamer partial flush triggers -> client 502/stream end.

Alex Chen: Quick mitigation proposal: rollback commit `0f3a1b7` on a canary pool and disable continuous-batching tunables for streaming routes. Can we patch config on prod pool without full deploy?

DeployBot: Patch available: `PATCH config/runtime/continuous_batching -> enabled: false` in cluster `redwood-prod-usw2-canary`. Requires approval.

Maria Gonzalez: Approving now. Do it. :thumbsup:

Anika Ramos: I'm taking oncall handoff in 15m; keep me posted on mitigation and customer impact.

Alex Chen: Executing patch on canary. Command:```bash
kubectl patch cm runtime-config -n redwood-prod --patch '{"data":{"continuous_batching":"false"}}'```
Patch applied at 1824501320.

Sam Patel: Rolling back the batching heuristics to previous stable commit on canary too: `git revert 0f3a1b7 && helm upgrade`. Kicking that at 1824501360.

IncidentBot: Canary checks: kv_cache_mem trending down after patch; batch latencies reduced to ~30ms; streaming cadence normalized for canary.

Tara (CS): Fyi, two paying customers (acct-5012, acct-7241) opened support tickets reporting truncated streaming and error spikes. CS team notified and customers placed on priority.

Alex Chen: Initiating staged rollout of patch to prod pools with traffic shaping — small percentage first. We'll watch `5xx_rate` and `streaming_token_intervals` in real time.

Lee Park: Noting observable: eviction rate initially spiked after rollback then stabilized, looks like pinned entries were misclassified by `0f3a1b7`. We'll need a followup to add a guard to prevent eviction of active prefixes.

Maria Gonzalez: Live numbers:
- Before mitigation: kv_cache_entries: 12.4M, mem: 89%
- Canary after patch: entries: 3.1M, mem: 42%
- Prod first wave (5%): errors dropped 78% in 10m, streaming stalls largely resolved.

Alex Chen: I'm increasing rollout to 25% now. Keeping canary paused for 10m observation window.

Anika Ramos: Handoff note: I'll own incident during my rotation. If rollout regresses, escalate to runtime oncall (Sam + Lee).

Sam Patel: One more mitigation we applied: reduced `max_batch_age_ms` from 25 -> 10 for streaming routes to limit partial flush windows. Command used:```json
{"streaming": {"max_batch_age_ms": "10"}}
``` That makes partial flush more aggressive but avoids long stalled cadences.

Alex Chen: Observed streaming partial-flush error logs:```text
[streamer] partial_flush_timeout: client=acct-7241 route=/v1/stream model=gpt-opus seq=#### status=502
[cache] eviction_attempt: key=prefix-xyz pinned=false last_access=12s
``` This pattern was common during the spike.

Tara (CS): Customer acct-7241 acknowledged improved behavior after our rollback, asked for ETA on full resolution. We told them 2 hours for full rollout and root-cause followup.

Maria Gonzalez: Next steps (short):
1) Complete staged rollout to 100% with monitoring baseline.
2) Postmortem: identify logic bug in `pin_proximity` algorithm (probable cause).
3) Add automated guard to prevent paging when eviction rate > threshold.
4) Re-run local fuzz tests for prefix distributions.

Lee Park: Requesting logs for suite: `kv_cache.eviction.*`, `batching.metrics.*`, `streamer.partial_flush.*` from 1824501000 -> 1824503000. I'll pull and start triage.

Alex Chen: Rollout to 100% complete at 1824503000. Metrics: error rate back to baseline, kv cache mem = 45%. Rolling restarts avoided.

IncidentBot: Severity lowered to P2 at 1824503050. Continue to monitor for 2h.

Anika Ramos: Taking over active coordination. I'll open a followup incident for the root-cause and schedule postmortem. TAGS: oncall, kv-cache, continuous-batching, streaming.

Sam Patel: For the postmortem I'll collect diffs and write a small repro harness to replicate the skewed prefix distribution that caused the bloom in entries.

Maria Gonzalez: Also adding an action: add a canary test that runs traffic with high prefix locality every deploy of batching heuristics.

Tara (CS): I'll send customer comms: summary + apology + link to status page, offer dedicated check-in if they want.

Lee Park: Locking down: create a short-term L0 fix in code that prevents pinning from being ignored when `last_access < 30s`. We'll ship in the next minor release after tests.

Alex Chen: Thanks team. If anything flips, @Anika and I are both paged. Otherwise we'll meet in 90m for postmortem planning. :white_check_mark:

DeployBot: Patch rollout logs: canary OK -> 5% OK -> 25% OK -> 100% OK. All checks green.

IncidentBot: Incident closed (mitigated) at 1824504120.

Anika Ramos: Closing notes for handoff: initial cause = batching heuristics change `0f3a1b7` interacting oddly with certain request-locality patterns -> cache entry blowup -> eviction thrash -> streaming partial flushes. Mitigation = rollback + disable continuous-batching + `max_batch_age_ms` temporary reduction. Followups assigned.

Maria Gonzalez: I'll own the RCA doc and link it to #postmortems once done.

Tara (CS): Customers updated. No SLA credits requested so far.

Alex Chen: Great work everyone.
